reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month since August 2026 (E-07); disputed bills are predominantly ACTUAL-read, not estimated (1785 vs 1240, E-02), ticket response stays within SLA (E-03), and no tariff change occurred (E-04/E-06). Evidence best supports a billing import validation rule change around August 2026 causing calculation errors in issued bills regardless of read type (matching the ACTUAL-read majority and surge timing), not a response-handling, tariff, or pure estimate-substitution problem; the field route completion shortfall (E-01) is a separate smaller contributor limited to the ESTIMATED-read subset.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-07). Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (vs 1785 ACTUAL-read, E-02), 1184 trace to AMI reads delivered on time but rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12). This traces to billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling=none (E-13); because firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report raw register values in units of 0.1 m3 while legacy v3.x meters report in whole m3 (E-14), BV-17's unscaled comparison misclassifies normal v4.2 consumption as anomalously high and rejects it at import, forcing estimate substitution that triggers disputes. This mechanism accounts for the ESTIMATED-read subset; the larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785) is not yet explained by it.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
